(1) Failure modes now covered by retraining  
- Local, subtle violations inside otherwise well‑formed answers:  
  • Exact counts/lengths: word counts, character counts, vowel totals.  
  • Fine‑grained lexical constraints: palindromes; no repeated letters; specific start/end letters; spelled‑out numbers vs digits.  
  • Ordering/sorting: alphabetical order of words, numbers by name, ascending numeric order with extra global constraint (e.g., prime sum).  
  • Micro‑formatting: lowercase vs capitalized, missing/extra punctuation, trailing spaces, forbidden whitespace in JSON, per‑line markers.  
  • Logical/conditional constraints across elements (e.g., include banana only if “yellow”; “blue” only if “sky”; specified tense/voice).

(2) Regions already robust  
- Clear, global failures on simple prompts (wrong type, obvious forbidden token, extra sentences/JSON keys) and cleanly satisfied simple constraints are reliably classified.

(3) High‑value regions to probe next  
- Longer, multi‑turn dialogues with evolving constraints.  
- Instructions mixing semantic correctness with subtle constraints (negations, “unless,” nested conditionals).  
- Tasks involving reasoning chains (math, logic) where format appears correct but deep content is wrong.

(1) Failure modes now covered by retraining  
- Multi‑turn “now modify the artifact” across many formats (tables, CSV, YAML/INI, HTML/XML/LaTeX, code) where the model:  
  • Applies no transformation, or only a subset of requested edits.  
  • Violates “only if / unless / except in X / only in Y” locality constraints.  
  • Mishandles interacting constraints (subset filters + numeric/string update + column/row freezing or reordering).  
  • Relies on surface structural mimicry while semantic/logical conditions are wrong (palindromes, ranges, substrings, positions, counts).

(2) Regions already robust / low information  
- Single‑turn exact‑copy vs clearly altered outputs.  
- Gross format violations or obviously wrong answer types.

(3) High‑value regions to probe next  
- Longer dialogues with 3–5 sequential transformations to the same artifact.  
- Cross‑artifact dependencies (edit code + narrative + config consistently).  
- Tasks where satisfaction depends on global invariants or cross‑row/section relations, not just local edits.
